Red Coral Italy gemstone has fascinated mankind since ancient ages. In almost all ancient civilizations and cultures, be it in ancient India, Egypt, Greece or Rome people believed that coral has various magical virtues. Jewelry made from Coral was a favorite amongst the rich as it was a means to exhibit their wealth.

Red coral grows from the skeletons of coral polyps, animals no larger than one millimeter. Their skeletons, made of calcium carbonate, pile up to form coral. It takes more than 100,000 years for coral to turn into a reef. Unlike other gemstones which are found on Earth crust, this gemstone is found naturally in the dark parts of deep Sea.

The Red Coral gemstone from Italy is believed to be a transformative, calming, and peaceful stone. It helps those who are trapped in negative thoughts about the past to break free and move on. Italian Red Coral Buying Guide

Check its Origin:

The Mediterranean Sea is the primary source of Italian red coral, particularly along the coastlines of Italy, Sardinia, and Sicily. These areas are well-known for producing some of the finest red coral specimens in the world. The coral colonies are typically found at depths ranging from 10 to 300 meters, and the coral branches are carefully harvested from underwater rocky formations by skilled divers.

Observe their Color:

The captivating and rich red color of the Italian red coral gemstone ranges from a warm, deep crimson to a vibrant fiery hue. For centuries, its vibrant color has made it highly sought after for jewelry and decorative purposes, symbolizing passion, vitality, and the enduring beauty of the Mediterranean sea.

Notice their Clarity:

Italian red coral gemstones are highly sought after due to their excellent clarity. The absence of significant inclusions, cracks, or blemishes in these gemstones allows for optimal light transmission and the display of their vivid red color. This exceptional clarity enhances the gem's visual appeal, allowing it to shine with mesmerizing intensity.

Examine their Inclusions:

The most noticeable inclusions in Italian red coral are often dendritic structures that resemble delicate, tree-like patterns, and these are desirable because they add to the gem's uniqueness and authenticity. While some inclusions may affect the clarity of the gemstone, they do not detract significantly from its value or beauty because they are regarded as a testament to the coral's organic origin and natural growth process, adding character to this precious gemstone.

See their Shape:

Italian Red Coral is cut in Oval or Capsule-shape for use in Red Coral stone Rings. Look for a regular shape and even surface.

Check the Carats:

For Italian Red Coral of gem quality, the raw Red Coral is divided and polished into smaller stones of variable carat weight. In general, Red Coral weighing between 7 and 15 carats are appropriate for jewelry. Because Red Coral is sold by weight, Red Coral prices are calculated per carat. Stones of comparable dimensions but distinct varieties vary greatly in price. The more carats and clarity Red Coral has, the higher its price.

Avoid Heated & Treated Red Coral

Due to treatments the Red Coral stone loses its natural composition and thus loses its natural frequency. These heated and treated Red Coral do not offer any healing benefits and should be avoided.

Check for Lab Certificate

It is recommended that you should purchase Italian Red Coral gemstones along a lab tested certificate which can determine its authenticity, treatment status and origin. How to Identify or Test Original & Authentic Red Coral Italy Stone?

Rudra Centre only deals with Vedic Astrology approved gemstones that are natural, untreated, and unheated. All our Red Coral are certified by reputable labs like GIA, GLI, IGI and IGITL.

Look for flaws along with inclusions. Use a magnifying glass with at least 10x magnification to examine the Red Coral carefully. Look for specks and blemishes, as they form with minute particles of other material. These flaws are strong evidence that a Red Coral is genuine. Lab-created (fake) Red Coral have no inclusions of this nature, and neither do natural Red Coral, but if you find flaws, then your Red Coral is genuine.

Examine the gemstone for air bubbles. Essentially, lab-created Red Coral are glass that has undergone a process similar to that which forms natural Red Coral. Since they are made of glass, they retain miniscule air bubbles after formation. If there are bubbles within the Red Coral, it is not genuine. Be sure to inspect your Red Coral from every angle by turning it over. There is a possibility that bubbles of air will only be evident from a single angle.

Look at how light is reflected by the Red Coral. Turn off all the lights and shine your flashlight on the Red Coral. If it is genuine, it will only reflect light of the same hue as itself. If it is a fake, made of glass, it will reflect colors other than the natural color of the gem.

Clean natural Red Coral Italy gemstone with a soft polishing cloth and plain water. Rinse with a mild solution of soap and water. Do not soak. Avoid sudden temperature changes.

Avoid using commercial jewelry cleaners as they can damage the gemstone.
